problems.title: The reported finite two-dimensional congestion problem is regularized in code but singular in the mathematical definition
problems.source_location: Latest arXiv v3, Appendix F.4, PDF p. 23; current author parametric_pushforward/obstacles.py, congestion_cost.
analysis: In two dimensions, a smooth density positive near a point makes the near-diagonal contribution of \(|x-y|^{-2}\) proportional to \(\int_0^\epsilon r^{-1}\,dr=+\infty\). Removing exact empirical self-pairs does not remove this population singularity. The implementation uses denominator \(|x-y|^2+1\), a bounded regularized functional, so its finite numerics do not evaluate the literal displayed objective.
result: This is a supported local finding within the stated source/formulation scope. Its effect on the paper's aggregate experimental results remains unmeasured.
assumptions: The finding is restricted to the identified paper version and identified released component; published experiment provenance is not inferred from public code alone.
problems.impact_rationale: The literal two-dimensional functional is singular and the released version is a different regularization, but the underlying density-path method and finite reported calculations are not refuted. This local specification issue is Minor.
problems.existing_correction_status: A local correction or qualification is proposed where specified; author adoption is not established.

problems.title: Absolute continuity alone does not justify the diffeomorphic static formulation
problems.source_location: Section 2.1, PDF p. 3; Section 3.1 and Theorem 1, PDF p. 5 (diffeomorphic endpoint maps).
claim: Section 2.1, PDF p. 3, restricts the distributions to Lebesgue-dominated densities. The introduction, p. 1, describes a continuous velocity field. Section 3.1, p. 5, defines the static endpoint maps to be orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms and infers that this set is nonempty from the existence of endpoint densities. Theorem 1 then equates the dynamic problem (6) with the diffeomorphic static problem (11).

Appendix B, latest arXiv v3 PDF pp. 14–15, starts the forward direction by treating a dynamic local minimizer as a \(C^1\) diffeomorphic flow. Absolute continuity of the endpoint measures and continuity of the velocity do not establish this flow regularity.
analysis: Starting from uniform density on \([-1,1]\), continuous velocity \(v(x)=2\operatorname{sign}(x)\sqrt{|x|}\) sends nonzero particles to \(\operatorname{sign}(x)(\sqrt{|x|}+t)^2\). At positive time the endpoint density has two separated support components and finite action. A global diffeomorphism maps the initial connected support to a connected set, so no such diffeomorphism matches that endpoint. The example belongs to the broad weak continuity-equation class, while stronger continuously differentiable flow assumptions exclude it.
result: Endpoint absolute continuity and continuous velocity do not establish the claimed unrestricted diffeomorphic admissibility/equivalence. Matching stronger flow regularity changes the problem scope and must be explicit.
assumptions: The finding is restricted to the identified paper version and identified released component; published experiment provenance is not inferred from public code alone.
problems.impact_rationale: The endpoint assumptions do not ensure the nonempty diffeomorphic map class required by the central static/dynamic equivalence theorem. The support-topology counterexample exposes a substantial missing admissibility hypothesis, warranting Major.
problems.existing_correction_status: A local correction or qualification is proposed where specified; author adoption is not established.

problems.title: Appendix A’s optimality equations need correction, while fixed-endpoint minimizer equivalence can be retained
problems.source_location: Latest arXiv v3, Section 2.2, PDF p. 4; Appendix A, optimization problems (17)–(18) and displayed KKT equations, PDF p. 14.
claim: Section 2.2, PDF p. 4, and Appendix A, Eqs. (17)–(18), latest arXiv v3 PDF p. 14, relate a deterministic continuity-equation action with Fisher information to stochastic control with diffusion coefficient \(\sigma^2/2\), using \(\Phi=S+(\sigma^2/2)\log\rho\).
analysis: With \(v=\nabla S\) and positive potential action, the variational Hamilton–Jacobi equation has the opposite displayed signs for the potential/Fisher terms; the stochastic multiplier equation also requires its diffusion Laplacian. However, setting \(a=\sigma^2/2\) and \(u=v+a\nabla\log\rho\) changes the integrated action only by a fixed endpoint-entropy term under the stated regularity and boundary conditions. Thus the appendix equations need correction while the fixed-endpoint minimizer correspondence can survive.
result: The local optimality-equation derivation needs correction. The entropy-boundary argument preserves fixed-endpoint minimizers under its regularity and boundary restrictions.
assumptions: The finding is restricted to the identified paper version and identified released component; published experiment provenance is not inferred from public code alone.
repair: Use corrected variational equations and prove the action identity including its endpoint-entropy term, with the density regularity and boundary conditions stated explicitly.
problems.impact_rationale: The appendix equations need local variational corrections, while the fixed-endpoint minimizer equivalence survives through an entropy-boundary identity; Minor reflects that preserved result.
problems.existing_correction_status: A local correction or qualification is proposed where specified; author adoption is not established.

impact_rationale: Major is reserved here for the substantial failure of the stated central mathematical argument identified in p2. This does not establish a reversal of the experimental results.
